# AML evidence packet — draft v1

This curated input is not a comprehensive review. Every method receives the same UTF-8 file. Summaries are original paraphrases. Bibliographic metadata and abstracts were checked through the public NCBI ID converter and PubMed EFetch on 2026-10-05. Selected studies predate 2025. Co-Scientist's validated candidates and generated proposals are not input or the only correct answers.

## Research question

Propose one mechanistically specific AML drug-repurposing hypothesis using a drug approved for a different indication. Specify the biological context, supported premises and speculative bridges, selectivity and translational limitations, and a discriminating preclinical validation strategy with a falsifying outcome. State the original indication and distinguish verified facts from prior knowledge that needs checking. Do not present an established AML regimen as a new repurposing discovery. This adapts the Co-Scientist objective rather than reproducing a private original prompt.

## S1 — A leukemia-stem-cell metabolic dependency

Lagadinou et al. (2013), *BCL-2 inhibition targets oxidative phosphorylation and selectively eradicates quiescent human leukemia stem cells*. Cell Stem Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.stem.2012.12.013`; PMID: `23333149`; PMCID: `PMC3595363`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23333149/).

Functionally defined leukemia stem cells in the studied specimens frequently had low reactive-oxygen-species levels and elevated BCL-2. BCL-2 inhibition reduced oxidative phosphorylation and affected quiescent leukemia stem cells. This motivates investigating specific dependencies and selectivity. It does not establish that an arbitrary mitochondrial inhibitor has an acceptable therapeutic window or works across every AML context.

## S2 — Resistant cells are not necessarily the same stem-cell population

Farge et al. (2017), *Chemotherapy-Resistant Human Acute Myeloid Leukemia Cells Are Not Enriched for Leukemic Stem Cells but Require Oxidative Metabolism*. Cancer Discovery. DOI: `10.1158/2159-8290.CD-16-0441`; PMID: `28416471`; PMCID: `PMC5501738`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28416471/).

Residual cells in cytarabine-treated models were not consistently enriched for immature, quiescent leukemia stem cells. They displayed oxidative-metabolism-associated properties, including mitochondrial and fatty-acid-oxidation-related features. Altering that state changed treatment response in the studied settings. This cautions against equating all residual disease with the ROS-low population in S1. These model findings do not establish clinical efficacy of a new compound.

## S3 — An established mechanistic comparator

Pollyea et al. (2018), *Venetoclax with azacitidine disrupts energy metabolism and targets leukemia stem cells in patients with acute myeloid leukemia*. Nature Medicine. DOI: `10.1038/s41591-018-0233-1`; PMID: `30420752`; PMCID: `PMC7001730`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30420752/).

The report connected venetoclax–azacitidine treatment to changes in leukemia-stem-cell energy metabolism, including TCA-cycle and oxidative-phosphorylation effects, using patient-associated observations and experimental follow-up. It provides an established comparator. Repeating this combination is not a new repurposing proposal. The findings cannot be transferred directly to another drug or treated as universal randomized comparative efficacy evidence.

## S4 — Differentiation as a distinct outcome

Sykes et al. (2016), *Inhibition of Dihydroorotate Dehydrogenase Overcomes Differentiation Blockade in Acute Myeloid Leukemia*. Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.cell.2016.08.057`; PMID: `27641501`; PMCID: `PMC7360335`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27641501/).

DHODH inhibition promoted myeloid differentiation in experimental AML systems and affected disease-related endpoints in the investigated models. This connects metabolism with differentiation and supplies an alternative to nonspecific cell killing. It does not establish that every approved drug affecting this pathway reproduces the result or achieves suitable exposure and selectivity.

## Evidence boundaries

- Specify context and endpoint; distinguish bulk-cell effects, stem-cell effects, and differentiation.
- Approval, original indication, exposure and selectivity facts outside these summaries need explicit verification. Label recollections as unverified prior knowledge.
- Include normal-cell and mechanistic comparators; a pathway link alone is insufficient evidence of efficacy.
- State what would disconfirm the proposed drug–mechanism–context relationship.
- Absence from Co-Scientist's reported positive candidates is not an incorrect-answer label.


Proposed answer (the answer to evaluate):
Teriflunomide-driven pyrimidine depletion differentiates salvage-poor, cytarabine-residual AML

Hypothesis and premises. At clinically attainable unbound exposure, teriflunomide will cause DHODH-dependent pyrimidine depletion, clonal differentiation and durable loss of leukemia propagation in oxidative cytarabine-residual AML with insufficient compensatory salvage, while relatively sparing normal progenitors. Oxidative dependence of residual cells [S2] and differentiation after DHODH inhibition [S4] support separate premises, not their drug-specific conjunction. Oxidative metabolism does not establish DHODH dependence. Residual cells must not be equated with ROS-low stem cells [S1,S2]. Venetoclax–azacitidine remains an established comparator [S3]. Teriflunomide’s approval for relapsing multiple sclerosis, DHODH pharmacology and uridine bypass are unverified prior knowledge.

Salvage-capacity correction. Baseline isotope fractions measure usage, not reserve. Prospectively classify paired untreated/residual samples before teriflunomide testing: high respiration remains ATP-linked oxygen consumption ≥75th percentile of an independent untreated-AML reference. Measure labeled-uridine incorporation and UTP/CTP maintenance during matched, viability-preserving genetic DHODH repression under measured physiological marrow uridine. Define poor reserve as pools <80% of baseline and competent reserve as ≥90%; these are design assumptions, not validated biomarkers. Retain intermediate and low-respiration samples for continuous analyses. Bidirectional gain/loss of experimentally validated salvage components, with vector/non-targeting controls and within-genotype vehicle arms, must shift flux, pools and drug response in opposite directions. Paired untreated samples distinguish residual-state enrichment from generic salvage dependence. These causal and context-specific predictions remain speculative.

Verification gates. The packet cannot resolve teriflunomide/leflunomide AML precedent or provide numerical human exposure bounds. Audit that literature against the precise compensatory-salvage/residual-cell prediction before any novelty claim. Verify approval, target selectivity, protein binding and approved-dose unbound peak/AUC profiles. Select culture and xenograft schedules reproducing 0.25-, 0.5- and 1-fold verified concentration–time profiles, measuring free medium drug and unbound marrow exposure. No numerical dose or clinical feasibility is asserted here; activity exceeding verified human bounds cannot support repurposing.

Mechanistic controls. Include vehicle, genetic DHODH repression, venetoclax–azacitidine and a non-DHODH cytostatic control matched for division slowing. Measure DHODH activity, dihydroorotate/orotate, nucleotide pools, respiration and viability before differentiation. Preventive uridine rescue is interpretable only if it restores nucleotide pools. Track initially immature, genotype-positive leukemic clones using lineage tracing, morphology, maturation markers and absolute counts, excluding selective blast death or normal-cell expansion. Test normal CD34-positive progenitors under matched protein, uridine and proliferative conditions, including colony recovery.

Quantitative decision rules. Require ≥20-percentage-point day-seven clonal differentiation and ≥3-fold lower leukemia-propagating frequency versus vehicle; require ≥80% normal colony recovery at threefold minimal effective exposure, an ex vivo margin only. The salvage-by-treatment interaction must be ≥20 percentage points, defined as the between-stratum difference in donor-level drug-minus-vehicle differentiation. Eighteen independent evaluable donors per stratum targets approximately 80% power against zero for a true 20-point interaction, assuming 20-point standard deviation and two-sided α=0.05; adjust enrollment using blinded variance estimates. This powers the interaction test, not the entire joint success criterion. Thresholds require independent replication.

Propagation-artifact correction. Randomize and blind exposure-matched xenografts. Before equal-viable-leukemic-cell limiting-dilution transplantation, verify intracellular and extracellular drug clearance below experimentally established no-effect thresholds and allow prespecified drug-free recovery while measuring division and death kinetics. Measure early marrow homing; use direct marrow implantation if homing differs. Serial transplantation tests durability. Persistent division delay, impaired homing or drug carryover cannot establish differentiation-associated loss of propagation.

Falsification and limitations. Adequate target engagement and depletion without either AML endpoint rejects the full claim. Salvage manipulations changing flux/pools but not sensitivity, or a precisely estimated interaction below the specified minimum, reject the subgroup mechanism. Effects persisting after confirmed preventive nucleotide rescue, or absent with matched genetic depletion, contradict DHODH mediation. Failure of the normal-cell margin or human-exposure gate rejects selectivity or feasibility. Off-target mitochondrial injury, cytostasis and maturation without durable functional change remain alternatives. Dynamic marrow nutrients, heterogeneous salvage and xenograft/colony-model limitations leave clinical safety, post-cytarabine recovery and efficacy unresolved.

Ranked proposal:
Teriflunomide-driven pyrimidine depletion differentiates salvage-poor, cytarabine-residual AML
